headline: Highest risk is CrewAI’s default shared-memory, filesystem, and broad egress creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action hazards; LightZero adds little direct risk but does not isolate the pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and uses shared memory by default, so attacker-controlled content in files can influence its tool use. LightZero has no ingestion surfaces, so it is not a direct injector, but the pair still has a plausible shared-filesystem bridge if orchestrated together.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same working directory
IF CrewAI is configured to parse file contents as instructions or context
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable automatic file ingestion in CrewAI
Add a manual review step before CrewAI consumes any file
Run LightZero in a read-only sandbox
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI handles API keys and broad network egress, while LightZero has no filesystem or network surfaces. If both share a workspace, CrewAI can read sensitive files and transmit them to model providers or tools; LightZero is not the leak source, but it does not prevent the path.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in CrewAI's working directory
IF CrewAI tool integrations or model providers receive file contents
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Mount CrewAI on a minimal input-only directory
Disable unnecessary tool integrations
Use separate credentials for each agent
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, but LightZero has no write, shell, or network capabilities. There is no meaningful overlapping mutable resource in the profiles, so direct capability conflict is limited to unusual orchestration choices.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator maps both agents onto the same writable directory
IF LightZero is wrapped with additional write-capable tools not shown in the profile
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Avoid concurrent writes from CrewAI
Keep LightZero read-only
Use file locks if a shared artifact is unavoidable
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI is a multi-agent orchestration framework with shared memory, so its outputs can become authoritative inputs to downstream steps. LightZero is a game-playing system and does not verify CrewAI's claims, making a mistaken CrewAI output likely to cascade if the pair is chained without a human check.
conditions: IF LightZero consumes CrewAI-generated text or decisions as input
IF no explicit verification step is inserted between the agents
mitigations: Insert a human approval gate
Require LightZero to ignore free-form CrewAI claims
Log and compare intermediate outputs
Use structured schemas instead of prose
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI touches developer-passed crew data and API keys, while LightZero touches no data classes and has no residency or retention profile. The pair shows no explicit compliance mismatch in the profiles, but CrewAI's handling of secrets means any shared sensitive data should still be minimized.
conditions: IF regulated data is passed into CrewAI's crew context
IF retention or residency requirements apply to API-key-bearing prompts or logs
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in crew prompts
Review logging settings
Use redacted test data
Separate credentials from content
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
